If you want the image to be linked, then simply insert a link using Markdown into the sidebar text and target the link using the same technique in the guide.

Okay, the guide I referred to shows you how to use the nth-of-type selector. We need to use this because we have no way of uniquely identifying user-made links (with classes or IDs).

  1. Insert a link into the sidebar text using Markdown, like `a link.

  2. Style the link using .titlebox .usertext-body .md > p:nth-of-type(n) a, where n depends on where your link is in the sidebar. If it is the very first thing you can also use p:first-of-type.

In my mind Montana is fairly conservative, but strongly independent. Given the geographic location and the mindset of the people, how do you see cannabis legalization going forward?

This is an excellent question! Personally I have no real idea how we are going to move forward. The state has had, in my opinion, a really screwed up history with our current medical marijuana status. I am not sure how much you know but to sum it up we passed medical marijuana laws, everything was fine for a few years and then we hit the green card boom. During this time doctors started to become more willing to give recommendations. I thought this was a great step forward since we are more conservative. Until the traveling pot caravans started, which was a great idea but very poorly executed. They were large groups of doctors (most were from different states) that gave recommendations and people that helped the "patients" sign up for their cards on the spot. Like I said it was a great idea. The problem was that they signed up anyone regardless of who they were and their medical history. The whole process took about 5 minutes start to finish and they signed up thousands of people in no time at all. This left a very bad taste in the mouths of conservative Montanans that already disagreed with medical marijuana. Then to top it all off they were ran by a douche that had no respect for what he was doing, where he was, the people he worked with, the local law enforcement, the people he signed up and was basically in it for the cash only, in my opinion. He would smoke in places that asked him not too, was very hot headed, quick to yell and scream at anyone (I worked in a call center where I had personal experience with this over the phone and heard stories of him going to the local offices). At one point he even called in and got charged for a bomb threat at a Verizon store for issues with his service. I, and a lot of us up here, blame him personally for the reform laws and downfall that came after. Store fronts were shut down and not able to be in business by the reform, providers were hardly able to provide anything and couldn't really charge for what they supplied, doctor's couldn't really give recommendations with out running the risk of losing their license to pratice and in one day Montana was hit with one of the largest statewide federal raids in history. We now have a barely functional medical law that is in constant debate and I see no end in sight. In fact at this moment a local car dealership owner is starting a petition to end all medical marijuana laws and go back to being 100% illegal. He tried this previously but didn't get enough signatures to get it on the ballot so he has started earlier this year.
It is with a heavy heart that I make this comment... I feel for Montanans everywhere who are deserving and needing medical MJ.

Thanks for the answer! I didn't know the about the medical ordeal you guys are having to deal with. Here in IL we legalized medical in 2013, but it has yet to be enacted and the list of eligible illnesses is very restrictive. If I recall correctly, we still have quite a bit of work to do before it is enacted, and then there will be some time for dispensaries to get set up (can't home grow). The law will automatically expire in 2018. This bill was supposed to be a 'test run.' At this pace we will only get to see how it works for about 1.5 years, which is not enough time and was not the intent of the bill.
